styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: The Louvre, Notre-Dame and the old streets of Le Marais.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Markets, bakeries and long bistro lunches.

styles.label: Romance
styles.blurb: Seine walks, candlelit dinners and Montmartre at dusk.

stays.why: Central and walkable. Close to Notre-Dame, the Pompidou and good cheap food. Lively at night.
Classic Paris feel by the river. Good for cafés, bookshops and the Luxembourg Gardens.
Closest to the Louvre, the Tuileries and big department stores. Best metro links for short trips.
Quieter and often cheaper. Village feel around Sacré-Cœur, but longer rides to the centre.

food: Try a basic bistro lunch: many places do a fixed 'formule' of two or three courses for about €18–28.
Buy picnic food at a street market or bakery: baguette, cheese and fruit for under €10.
Order the plat du jour at lunch. It is usually cheaper than the same dish at dinner.
Tap water is free and safe. Ask for 'une carafe d'eau' instead of bottled water.
Book popular dinner spots a few days ahead. Many small places are closed one or two weekdays; check on the day.
more_time: Swap a city day for Versailles: take RER C, then walk the palace and gardens. Allow a full day.
Travelling with kids? Swap a museum morning for Disneyland on RER A. Book tickets ahead.
Want a slower day? Ride a Vélib' bike along the Seine and stop at a market for lunch.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the big sights, a market lunch and an evening on the Seine without rushing.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near 7°C and about 13 rain days. Pack a warm coat and waterproof shoes.
February: still cold, highs near 10°C, about 11 rain days. Quiet museums and shorter queues.
March: mild at about 12°C but wet, around 13 rain days. Bring an umbrella.
April: pleasant highs near 16°C, about 10 rain days. Good for parks and long walks.
May: warm at about 19°C, around 13 rain days. Pack layers and a light rain jacket.
June: warm and bright, highs near 23°C, about 12 rain days. Long evenings outdoors.
July: hottest month, highs near 26°C, about 9 rain days. Busy; book sights ahead.
August: warm at about 25°C, around 10 rain days. Some small shops close for holidays.
September: lovely at about 22°C, around 9 rain days. A strong month for walking.
October: cooler at about 17°C, around 12 rain days. Bring a jacket and umbrella.
November: cool at about 11°C, around 12 rain days. Indoor sights and cafés suit best.
December: cold, highs near 9°C, about 13 rain days. Dark early; dress warm for evenings out.

climate_guide.summary: Mild, changeable weather with rain in every month. Summers are warm, not hot; winters are cold and grey.

items.title: Best months: May to September
items.text: Highs around 19–26°C. Long daylight and the best odds of dry, pleasant days.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: About 9–13 rain days every month. Showers are often short; carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Cold winters
items.text: December to February highs of 7–10°C and lows near 2°C. Warm coat, scarf and layers.

items.title: Warm, not hot, summers
items.text: July peaks near 26°C. Comfortable for walking, but book popular sights ahead in peak season.

items.title: Pack layers
items.text: Mornings and evenings are cooler than midday. A light jacket works most of the year.

items.title: Wear good shoes
items.text: You will walk a lot on cobbles and stone. Waterproof shoes help on wet days.

transit.best: Walk in the centre and use the Métro for longer hops.

modes.text: The Métro and RER cover the whole city. A single ticket is about €2.50; weekly Navigo passes are good value.
Buses use the same tickets. Slower than the Métro but scenic.
Metered taxis with flat fares from the airports. Uber, Bolt and G7 apps work everywhere.
Driving and parking in Paris are hard. A car is only useful for day trips.
Central Paris is compact and very walkable. Vélib' bikes are everywhere.
RER C goes to Versailles; Disneyland is on RER A.
